sonido/3e7b214:
Replace the linear-chain-only processing model with a compiled DAG:
ProcessingGraph holds topology (nodes, edges), compiles to an immutable
CompiledSchedule snapshot, audio thread executes the flat instruction
list with zero allocations.

Key design decisions (ADR-025):
- Two-object split (Tracktion pattern): ProcessingGraph for mutations,
  CompiledSchedule shared via Arc for lock-free audio thread access
- Buffer liveness analysis (JUCE pattern): register-allocation for audio
  buffers — 20-node linear chain uses 2 buffers, diamond uses 3
- Latency compensation: longest-path computation + CompensationDelay
  insertion on shorter parallel paths at each Merge node
- Click-free schedule swap: SmoothedParam crossfade (~5ms) when graph
  topology changes — both old and new schedules run during transition
- Cycle detection at connect() time via DFS reachability, defensive
  Kahn sort validation at compile() time

Node types: Input, Output, Effect (per-node bypass crossfade), Split
(fan-out), Merge (fan-in summing). ProcessStep instruction set:
WriteInput, ProcessEffect, SplitCopy, ClearBuffer, AccumulateBuffer,
DelayCompensate, ReadOutput.

GraphEngine in sonido-io wraps ProcessingGraph with from_chain() for
backward-compatible migration from ProcessingEngine — output is
numerically identical for linear topologies (verified by test).

Entire graph module is no_std compatible (alloc only) for Daisy Seed /
Hothouse embedded targets. 34 tests covering mutations, cycle rejection,
compilation, buffer efficiency, execution correctness, diamond summing,
schedule swap crossfade, and ProcessingEngine parity.

perennials/3ebd3fa:
The sheet can now wash this hour's computed shade over itself: one ray
per cell (40x56) against the same crowns and land the bed lines march,
painted into a cell-sized canvas and softened by the browser's upscale
plus a blur filter. Black, not ink, because ink flips light in the dark
theme and shade darkens in either; null below the horizon, because night
is not shade and the line says which. A Draw-the-shade toggle with the
hour slider appears on the sheet only once her latitude and span exist,
and the wash line prints its basis and how much of the sheet still gets
sun. shadeCells is pinned in rules: the bank fixture's bed cell is
washed at winter noon, open ground is not, and night draws nothing.

The drawings gain their craft in the same pass. A scale bar appears the
moment a span exists — a 1-2-5 round length near a fifth of the sheet
(scaleBarFor, rules-tested for both), on the plan and the exported page.
Bed washes pool at their edges with one wide soft stroke under the pen
line. Every SVG sheet (plan, elevation, export) takes the same paper
tooth from lib/paper.ts's turbulence recipe. The elevation adopts the
section drawing's line-weight convention — near the cut full-weight,
beyond it stepped back by depth — on screen and in the exported band.
And when the year-scrubber plays, tokens crossfade instead of strobing,
under prefers-reduced-motion.
perennials/3e64236:
The bloom-succession wheel the kept list already reads now mounts on the
yard over its placed plants, one row per distinct plant: the printed
bands, her sepia marks above them, per-slot counts and the year's gaps
named. BloomCalendar gains a context prop that swaps only the copy's
subject (you've kept / placed here); the records draw identically.

Two lines ride under it, each scoped to what our data can claim. The
pollinator famine (visitorGaps, lib/phenology.ts): slots where something
is recorded in bloom and none of the blooming plants has a recorded
flower visitor — a slot where nothing blooms at all is the calendar's
own verdict and is not claimed twice, and when visitors are recorded for
nobody the coverage sentence stands alone rather than dressing that
silence up as a famine. And the divergence aggregate: how many placed
plants her marks put in bloom outside their printed band, her yard
teaching the record, neither side called wrong.

Rules pin the famine's edges: bloom without a visitor is the only gap,
her mark alone brings a plant's visitors into a slot, her recorded
visitors count through ACCESS like a source's, and zero coverage is
never presented as a famine list.
perennials/3ec0ac6:
plants.json was never reaching Cache Storage. `cache.put(url, res.clone())` tees
the response stream, and with the three data fetches in flight together Chrome
cannot keep the 8.9 MB branch fed: put() rejects with "Cache.put() encountered a
network error" for plants.json while quietly succeeding for facets.json and
meta.json. I was swallowing the error.

It failed in the worst way available. Airplane mode still worked, so the fix I
shipped this morning looked correct, because the browser's own HTTP cache was
covering for the missing entry. I then raised max-age from 5 minutes to an hour,
which widened the window in which the bug is invisible. An hour after her last
visit, that entry goes stale and the garden gets an empty app.

Read the bytes once with arrayBuffer(), cache a fresh Response built from them,
and parse the same bytes. No clone, no tee. And log the failure instead of
swallowing it, because a silent one here is indistinguishable from success right
up until she is standing in a field with no signal.
site/3e9f201:
Opening a project left most of the controls dead. Up, down and A only ever
acted on the select screen, and the right d-pad key was a bare div with no
handler, no role and no tabIndex, so it did nothing on any screen. Only B
and left worked, both wired to Back.

Give the four keys a job on detail. Up and down scroll the body. Left and
right walk the link rail at the top right, which opens focused on the demo
when a project has one and on the source otherwise. A clicks whatever is
focused, and its caption reads OPEN instead of SELECT there. Left still
falls through to Back when a project has no links at all, so the hidden
projects keep their escape hatch. Arrow keys and Enter mirror the buttons;
none of them are synth note keys, so the playable detail screens are safe.

DetailScreen renders the rail from the same detailLinksOf() the hook indexes
into, so the render order and the focus index cannot drift apart. Every d-pad
key now goes through one DpadButton, which is what stops another one shipping
without a handler.

Scrolling accumulates against its own target rather than calling scrollBy:
Chrome resolves a smooth scrollBy against the live mid-animation offset, so
two quick taps of down scrolled one step instead of two. Caught by driving
the built site in headless Chrome, where the unit test's stubbed scrollBy
had hidden it.
